Zoe R: Quick sync — we need a crisp benchmark playbook for quantized runs (FP8/INT8/4-bit). Things to nail: kernel selection determinism, batching heuristics, KV cache warmup, calibration pass, power limits (thermal/power caps), tokenization parity, and fair baseline. Proposal below.

Matt H: +1. Concrete checklist suggestion:
- fix hardware & power cap
- freeze driver/CUDA/cuDNN
- single tokenizer commit
- identical model weights (pre-quant and post-quant mapping)
- deterministic kernel selection or record chosen kernel
- warmup tokens & KV states defined

Nisha K: For warmup, let's do two modes:
1) cold-start latency: no KV warmup, single-request latency
2) warmed KV throughput: run N_warm=2048 tokens across representative prompts, then measure steady-state throughput for M=10000 tokens
Always report both.

Sam L: Agree. Also specify batching shapes: report per-request latency and batched throughput for batch sizes [1,4,8,16]. Use sequence lengths [32,128,512] and report percentiles (p50/p95/p99).

Liya W: On kernel selection: toolchain picks kernels by heuristics. For fairness we should record actual kernel variants used and include a forced-run where we pin kernels to the same family across compares. Example env to force kernel (runtime dev-only):
```
export REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINT="int8_fast_kv"
./run_bench --model mymodel --quant int8
```
Run auto + pinned and show delta.

perf-bot: reminder: when posting results include these fields: hardware SKU, driver, CUDA, power cap (W), temp, batch shapes, seq len, tokenizer commit, model SHA, quant config, kernel trace file path, latency percentiles, throughput tokens/s, quality metrics (LL/perplexity or downstream metric).

Matt H: Calibration behaviour — for INT8/4-bit we need an explicit calibration pass on a held-out representative corpus (suggest 1k–2k sequences). Record calibration steps, calibration data seed, and the per-layer scale stats.

Nisha K: Also log any layer folding or per-channel vs per-tensor quant differences. Quantization changes numeric behavior — always include a delta table: QoR (perplexity/ROUGE/etc) vs tokens/s.

Zoe R: Tokenization parity: freeze tokenizer binary + vocab. Use the same tokenization pipeline for float baseline and quantized runs. If tokenization changes, results are invalid.

Sam L: On power limits: use two settings: default (no cap) and constrained (cap to X% of TDP, e.g., 70%). Report both — quantization sometimes hides power-related thermal throttling.

Liya W: KV cache details: report whether prefix KV caching is enabled, and measure the KV memory bandwidth and hit/miss behaviour. For recurrent workloads include a trace of KV growth and the average per-token KV eviction cost.

Matt H: Repro tips: run each cell 3 times, discard first (warmup) run for steady-state, and include CI artifacts: raw perf logs + kernel traces + calibration dumps. Use consistent random seed for sampling prompts.

Zoe R: Action items:
- Sam: add a run template + CI job that enforces the checklist (batch shapes, seq lengths, warmup tokens) — due EOD Wed
- Nisha: write the calibration procedure doc + example script (1k sample set) — due Thu
- Matt: add kernel trace collection to bench harness + schema for the kernel choice table — due Fri

perf-bot: queued bench run 1809124000. Will post summary when finished. :rocket:

Sam L: I'll put an example output table in the bench notebook with both accuracy and perf columns. Keep thread as single source of truth for methodology.

Zoe R: Thanks all — aim for a standard artifact so dedicated/beta teams can reproduce perf regressions consistently. :white_check_mark:
